newsitem.title: UK: Arbitrage rescues LIFFE cocoa from lows.
newsitem.headline: Arbitrage rescues LIFFE cocoa from lows.

text.p: Rallying New York cocoa futures rescued London from nine-month lows on Wednesday, pulling the key March LIFFE contract back to its comfortable range, traders said.
"It's really New York that pulled us up from the lows," said one trader.

A stream of arbitrage deals, trade short covering and industry buying outpaced early selling, helping the March contract emerge from a session low of 899 stg. It closed at 912 stg a tonne, up six stg on the day.

The finish above the previous contract low of 903 stg was seen technically encouraging although heavy overhead supply would make further gains difficult to sustain unless the fundamental picture changed, traders said.

The day's turnover totalled 7,217 lots but included a large volume of AAs, crosses and switches. March/May traded at 20 and 21 stg, while March/Sept and May/Sept were bid at 60 and 40 stg respectively.
Traders said arbitrage between CSCE and LIFFE had narrowed to 86 stg at one stage from 97. At London's close, the March/March arbitrage was back to 93 stg.

Earlier in the day March cocoa slipped through crucial support at 903-900 area amid trade and origin sales and briefly touched 899 stg but was unable to find sell stops there and quickly bounced back.
Traders said London's prospects hinged on sterling's moves and a new rally in the UK currency amid stregthening economy signals could bring new pressure.
Technically the market has widened its range to 899 and 956 stg and a strong band of supply is coming in from 920 stg.
